subject: Surge forgiveness ladder and staged billing approach
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@brightshop.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Zhang <mike@brightshop.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:02:00Z
Subject: Emergency quota increase request

Hi Soojin,

We have a planned marketing push for Black Friday weekend that will start next Friday and run ~72 hours. Our traffic model indicates we will exceed our current quota by ~3x for a 36-hour window (mostly inference requests for product recommendations). We want to avoid throttling/latency that would hurt conversion.

Can Redwood temporarily raise our quota and provide a clear pricing plan for any overrun?

Two asks from our side:
- Immediate short-term uplift (2–3x) for the weekend with an explicit overrun pricing ladder we can accept now.
- A one-time discount or credit on incremental tokens for the surge period — this helps us keep economics intact while we scale.

I've attached a short traffic forecast and campaign timing (brightshop_traffic_plan.xlsx). If it helps, we can sign an addendum or PO for a provisional uplift.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can you share options by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Engineering, BrightShop
alex@brightshop.com
Attachment: brightshop_traffic_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@brightshop.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Emergency quota increase request

Hi Alex — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We can support this without a full contract amendment; below are two pragmatic paths that other customers have accepted for short, high-impact surges. Both preserve SLAs and limit Redwood exposure while giving BrightShop predictable unit economics.

Proposal A — Rapid uplift (fastest execution)
- Temporary quota uplift: 2.5x current quota for a 48-hour window starting on your confirmed start time.
- Billing: incremental usage during the window charged at list overrun rate, with a 15% discount applied to that incremental amount if you sign the attached Surge Addendum and PO.
- True-up: we will reconcile final usage and invoice after the campaign; payment due per normal terms.
- Operational: we can raise rate limits within 4 hours of signed PO and DocuSign.

Proposal B — Surge forgiveness ladder (more conservative)
- Step ladder: Tier 1 (up to 1.5x): no uplift surcharge, Tier 2 (1.5–2.5x): incremental billed at list rate, Tier 3 (>2.5x): higher incremental rate but capped exposure with a hard upper limit.
- Billing smoothing: we apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of incremental charges if you commit to a 3-month smoothing cadence after the event.
- Operational: gradual rate limit ramp recommended to avoid brief bursts that can trigger autoscale delays.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Tell us which option you prefer (A or B) and confirm your expected start time.
2) We’ll send a short DocuSign addendum (proposed_surge_addendum.docx) and a quick PO template for your procurement.

Internal note for Ben/Laura: if finance/legal require a stricter cap we should push Option B as default — it limits upside risk. Also will need product to pre-authorize the rate limit change.

I attached a one-page addendum draft for quick signature. If you want the fastest path, choose Proposal A and we’ll expedite the uplift.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed_surge_addendum.docx (document, 28KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Emergency quota increase request

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 15:30 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Internal note for Ben/Laura: if finance/legal require a stricter cap we should push Option B as default — it limits upside risk. Also will need product to pre-authorize the rate limit change.

Soojin — agree. Two quick operational asks from my side before we commit:
1) Finance needs a maximum exposure number (hard dollar cap) we can present to our revenue ops team. Can you get Product to confirm a ceiling that prevents runaway surcharges? If not achievable, we need Option B.
2) Offer structure — I recommend the following concession to close quickly: 10% off list overrun rate for incremental volume during the 48-hour uplift if BrightShop signs a 3-month smoothing commitment (simple letter of intent). That ties the discount to a post-event commitment and protects us.

Also Laura — can you review for any procurement language we should not accept (escrowed true-up, billing lag, PO acceptance window)? If we can accept the one-time credit + 3-month smoothing clause, I think this is a reasonable commercial compromise.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Alex Romero <alex@brightshop.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Mike Zhang <mike@brightshop.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Emergency quota increase request / Surge forgiveness ladder and staged billing approach

Hi Soojin & team — thanks for the quick options. We’ll take Proposal A (Rapid uplift) with one tweak: the 15% discount on incremental usage is acceptable only if we can cap our exposure at $35,000 for the event (we expect to stay well under that, but need the cap for procurement).

We can sign the addendum via DocuSign and will attach a PO this afternoon (BrightShop_PO_9876.pdf). If you can confirm rate-limit changes will be in effect within 4 hours of our PO + signed addendum, we are good to go.

Appreciate the responsiveness — we’ll sign and return shortly.

Best,
Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Engineering, BrightShop
Attachment: BrightShop_PO_9876.pdf (pdf, 90KB)
